EDIT, and the composer is the only thing that should set it — the
server never merges it into a preference behind the sender's back.

EmailEnvelopeView.description:
The caller's resolved email envelope: the greeting and signature that
would go out, which rung supplied each, the org's own signature for the
fallback story, the policy in force, and the insertable tokens.

This is the preview AND the composer's prefill in one call, resolved
through the same chain and the same dialect the send path uses. A UI
that previewed with its own regex would be a second implementation of
the rules, and the one thing a preview must never be is more generous
than the send.

org_signature.description:
The org's own signature (rendered), so a member can see what their
messages fall back to without an admin.

user_greeting.description:
The caller's own stored defaults, unrendered — the token form the
editor edits.

EmailMessage.description:
One persisted email message. `rfc_message_id` is unique per org and is
the idempotency key for inbound processing; `email_refs` carries the
RFC 5322 References chain (`references` itself is reserved SQL).

transport.description: Which transport adapter handled the message (postmark/smtp/…).

EmailSourceView.description: One rung of the resolution chain, as the ledger reports it.

EmailTokenView.description:
One placeholder the signature editor can insert, with the value it would
expand to for the caller RIGHT NOW.

label.description: Human label for the picker row.

value.description:
What it expands to for this caller, or `None` when their record has
no value for it — a token that would render empty says so here
instead of looking like a field the editor forgot.

EmbedResolution.description:
The allowlist decision plus (optionally) the provider's own oEmbed
embed HTML, fetched server-side. `html` is present only when
`fetch=true` and the provider endpoint answers 2xx.

html.description:
Sanctioned embed HTML straight from the provider's oEmbed endpoint.
Never client-supplied; only present when `fetch` was requested.

oembed_url.description: The percent-encoded oEmbed URL this resolution would fetch.

primary_label.description:
Human labels for the card: contact candidates carry both contact
names; client candidates carry the client name + vendor label.

EntityKind.description:
Which entity family a batch targets. One batch = exactly one kind; the
parent-before-child ordering across batches keeps foreign references
resolvable without cross-batch transactions. D2 remainder extends the
original client/site/contact family with boards, tickets, and time
entries: [`Self::import_order`] is the documented run-script order.

EntityMerge.description: An audited, undoable contact merge (the `ci_merges` split substrate).

EntityMergeCandidate.description:
A reviewable client/contact dedupe candidate (ADR 0003 visible
evidence). For contact candidates both ids are set; for client
reconciliation the candidate side is the VENDOR ORG
(`vendor_org_id`/`vendor_label`) and `candidate_entity_id` is NULL.

EntitySourceLink.description: A vendor record link for a contact (the CI2 link key generalized).

auto_merge_threshold.description:
The org's auto-merge threshold, surfaced inline (why was this
queued instead of auto-merged).

oneOf.description:
Suggestion-grade `decision_record_dedupe` judgment; `None` (silent
in the UI) whenever the decision model is unconfigured — ADR 0010.

allOf.description: IF1-IF3 mutation parameters (idempotency key / version).

minutes.description:
`adjust_minutes` only: the NEW effective minutes for the entry
(0..=current effective). The signed delta is derived here.

reason.description:
Required by `reject`, `flip_billable`, and `adjust_minutes`:
the human explanation that rides the audit row (V9). Omitting
it is a 422, not a silent write.

unbillable_reason.description: `flip_billable` only: required when flipping to non-billable.

work_type.description: `recategorize` only: a category slug from the org taxonomy.

EntryActionRequest.description:
The body of an entry action. One endpoint, one envelope, every
in-context edit — so the reason requirement, the audit row, the
pre-run guard, and the invoiced lock cannot be forgotten on one
branch.

oneOf.description: The adjustment row this write produced, when it produced one.

audit_action.description: The audit action name written to `audit_events` (V9).

disposition.description: The entry's current disposition after the write.

EntrySuggestion.description: Suggestion payload built from one `decision_billing_audit` row.

chip.description:
The suggested classification chip: how to interpret the audit.
`billable_false` = "looks non-billable", `billable_true` =
"looks billable". Derived from the `billable` answer's
threshold state — never auto-applied.

label.description: Human-readable chip text the UI renders (typed, no model prose).

mode.description: `shadow` rows drive nothing and are labeled as such.

verdicts.description:
The server's mechanical verdicts for this entry (Wave 41 lane 8), each
with the one action that clears it. Empty means clean — and empty for
an entry that is not visible in scope either, because RLS proves
visibility by absence, never by an error.

suggestions.description:
Empty when the surface is unconfigured or no answers exist —
the honest visibly-absent state.

EscalationStep.description: One escalation ladder step as stored (`sla_escalation_steps`).

notify_user_ids.description: Extra recipients beyond the ticket assignee.

EscalatorSpec.description:
Scheduled escalator spec (E): uplift bps per billing-annual
anniversary.

first_uplift_on.description:
First anniversary the uplift applies from (`None` = the anchor's
first full period).

bundle_version.description: Envelope schema version. Bump ONLY for breaking section reshapes.

sections.description: The export sections. Always fully serialized.

restricted_to.description:
Optional visibility restriction: when non-empty, only these users
(plus admins) can see the client. Opaque user-id references.

kind.description: Structured note taxonomy: internal | client_visible | in_house_update.

ExportContact.description: One contact row; `client_id`/`site_id` reference this bundle.

bundle_version.description: Envelope version of the produced bundle (mirrors the body).

download_url.description:
Self-contained relative URL carrying the signature + expiry; the
client prefixes its API origin. Works without a bearer token.

sha256.description: sha256 of the stored bytes (download integrity check).

size_bytes.description: Exact bundle byte size as stored.

ExportFieldValue.description: One typed custom-field value attached to any entity row.

entity.description:
Field-definition family the value belongs to (ticket | client |
contact | asset) — resolved from the definition at load time.

value.description: The typed value exactly as stored (JSONB passthrough).

ExportHistoryView.description:
One ledger row as /settings/export renders it. The signed link is
NEVER stored — rows carry content facts; links are minted fresh.

ExportSections.description:
Section container — all fields always present; empty org state is an
empty array, never an absent key.

custom_field_values.description:
Every custom-field VALUE in the org, flat across entity families —
the data plane the U5 manifest deliberately excludes. `entity` names
the family the field definition attaches to (ticket | client |
contact | asset); `entity_id` is the owning row.

customization.description:
The U5 customization-manifest sections, embedded verbatim — D1 is
the manifest's generalization, not its replacement.

org.description:
Org profile identity (volatile counters excluded — a restore
reseeds the ticket-number sequence from the imported tickets).

tickets.description:
Tickets with their comments nested. Parents (client/site/contact)
are referenced by id into the sections above.

ExportSite.description: One site row; `client_id` references `clients` in this bundle.

ExportTicket.description:
One ticket with its comment thread nested. Authorship is an opaque
user-id reference; the bundle never carries user records.

category.description:
Semantic category of the captured status (behavior binds to this,
never to the status label).

number.description: Human number (e.g. "MAR-12") — the bundle's stable ticket key.

ExportTimeEntry.description:
One time entry; `ticket_id` and `user_id` reference this bundle's
tickets and the org's live users respectively.

ticket_id.description:
`None` on project-scoped entries (Wave 39 lane 4): `phase_id`
scopes the entry instead.

ExternalDocUrlKind.description:
The closed external-document vocabulary. The classifier in `core-kb`
maps a URL to exactly one of these; `other` is the honest fallback for
any link that is neither SharePoint, OneDrive, nor Google Drive.

ExternalDocumentMutationResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for external documents.

ExternalLink.description:
A typed external URL bound to a subject (vendor / PO / PO line /
device asset). No polymorphic FK — the write path checks that the
subject row exists in the org.

carrier.description: Carrier that owns a tracking page (kind = tracking).

allOf.description: Instant-first mutation parameters (IF1).

identity_keys.description: CI3 deterministic identity signals (source GUID, serial, MACs, ...).

observed_fields.description: CI5 observed tier: feed-written, churns with its source.

tag.description: Display defaults for a freshly created canonical item.

FeedUpsertRequest.description: The feeder upsert input — lane 8's seam (NinjaOne / IT Glue / Auvik).

auto_merged.description: Auto-merged at/above the org confidence threshold.

contradictions.description: Observed values that contradict a curated value (never applied).

created_item.description: A fresh canonical row was created by THIS sync (no twin risk).

queued_candidates.description: Reviewable candidates queued for a human (visible evidence).

resolved_existing.description:
An existing item was deterministically resolved through identity
keys; no second row exists for this source record.

FeedUpsertResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response (IF2): item fields flattened at the top
level plus the additive feed-sync evidence and `mutation` metadata.

FieldDefView.description:
Wire view of one field definition; choice kinds carry their closed
option set so generated clients can render editors directly.

board_id.description: Owning board (`None` = org-wide; v1 always creates board-scoped).

options.description: Closed option set for select/multiselect; empty otherwise.

FieldKindWire.description:
The definition kinds (mirror of migration 0009's CHECK set). Kept as a
string-newtype wire enum so unknown kinds fail validation, not deserialization.

FieldResolution.description:
Per-field resolution: which side's value wins when the tickets
disagree. `"survivor"` (the default) keeps the survivor's value.

FilterOp.description:
Filter operators supported by the v1 compiled reports. Operand typing is
enforced through [`ValueType`] matches in the builder, so e.g. a bool
operand can never reach a timestamp column. The serde encoding is the
`snake_case` slug (`lt_eq`, `is_null`, …) stored specs carry.

FilterValue.description:
A typed filter operand. The variant must match the catalog
[`ValueType`] of the filtered column (`Int` covers both Int and BigInt
columns) — enforced by [`ReportSpec::validate`], so a mismatched
operand can never reach a bind. The serde encoding is the externally
tagged slug (`{"text": "p1"}`, `{"bool": true}`).

oneOf.description: RFC 3339 instant (chrono serde encoding).
`YYYY-MM-DD`.

description.description:
The description to write. The server will only take text the approver
saw: the factual suggestion it offered for this entry.

minutes.description:
Whole minutes to take off the END of the entry's window, not a new
total and not a delta on the duration. An overlap is a fact about when
the work happened, so the fix shortens the window and the duration
follows it. A trim only ever shortens: lengthening what a client is
billed is not an approver's call from a queue.

note.description: Free-text context recorded on the decision trail.

FixEntryRequest.description:
POST /api/time-entries/:id/fix — an approver applies one verdict's fix
to an entry that is still in the queue. At least one of `description` /
`minutes` is required; the entry stays `submitted` afterwards, because
clearing the objection is not approving it.

FixEntryResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response (IF2): the entry as it now reads, plus the
undo substrate. The client reconciles from the snapshot and never has to
guess what the server did to the minutes.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key. Absent
in legacy clients — purely additive. (Creates carry no version.)

name.description:
Name of the custom copy. Must not collide with an existing role
name (typed 409 `role_name_taken`).

allOf.description: Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key.

FxRateEntry.description: One `fx_rates` row: append-only; corrections add rows, never rewrite.

base_currency.description: 1 base major unit buys `rate` quote major units.

source.description: 'manual' for the built-in provider; managed feeds stamp their own.

FxReconciliationRow.description:
One `ops.v1_fx_reconciliation` row — the FX deliverable to the books
(FX7): original amount, rate, source/date, base equivalent, sync
target. The core records conversions that happened; realized/unrealized
gain-loss stays in the accounting system.

sync_target.description:
The accounting export target ('none' until a deployment configures
one — qbo-export-sync / xero-export-sync are per-deployment).

nudge_sent_at.description: When the EOD run nudged for this day, if it did.

from.description: Inclusive local-day start (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to yesterday.

user_id.description: Manager report only: whose days. Requires owner/admin.

container_paths.description: Mount points inside the Garage container.

s3_endpoint.description: S3 endpoint the API is configured against, when S3 mode is on.

volumes.description:
Named volumes in the shipped compose file (the compose project
prefix applies at runtime).

HeartbeatRequest.description:
POST /api/presence/heartbeat body. One heartbeat per viewer per entity
instance every ~30s; entries expire after 90s without one (TTL is
server-side, see `realtime::presence`).

editing.description: True while the caller is actively editing (vs. just viewing).

IncidentView.description: The storm group behind an incident ticket.

alert_count.description: How many alerts have collapsed into this ticket so far.

attributes.description: Provider-specific structured context (must be a JSON object).

correlation_key.description:
Storm grouping key; defaults to `dedup_key` when absent so
uncorrelated alerts each anchor their own incident.

dedup_key.description: Provider's per-event identity. REQUIRED: this is the replay gate.

occurred_at.description: When the condition started (defaults to receipt time).

IngestResponse.description: POST /api/alerts/ingest — outcome of one signed delivery.

oneOf.description:
Present for `incident_created` and `collapsed`; `None` when the
anchor ticket vanished before a replay answered.

status.description:
`incident_created` (this alert anchored a NEW incident ticket),
`collapsed` (folded into the still-open storm incident), or
`duplicate` (replayed dedup_key — the stored alert is returned,
nothing was written).

granted_capabilities.description:
Capability keys granted at install — a subset of the pinned
manifest's declared set. Unknown keys are rejected (closed
vocabulary).

version.description: Pin the adopted version; defaults to the entry's latest.

settings_schema.description: The pinned manifest's declared JSON-Schema (the render source).

artifact_kind.description:
The governance profile from the PINNED manifest (ADR 0009 §6):
`wasm` | `http_connector` — the roster-tab discriminator.

effective_permissions.description:
The effective permission keys the grants resolve onto (the
EXISTING matrix vocabulary — `tickets:read`, `financial:read`,
…). Informational; enforcement re-derives from the same matrix.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version (of the newly created project). Absent in legacy clients —
purely additive.

assignee_map.description:
Resolves template `assignee_key`s to user ids at instantiation
time; unmapped keys simply leave those tasks unassigned.

IntegrationLinkStatus.description: Per-connector link state as data (linked/unlinked + last touch).

InviteInfo.description:
The one-time setup token an admin delivers to the invitee (shown once;
only its sha-256 is stored).

allOf.description: Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key.

role.description: Builtin org role preset: owner, admin, dispatcher, senior_tech, technician, bookkeeper, auditor, read_only.

Invoice.description:
The billing document. Derives from exactly one contract; `currency`
and `total_minor` come from the contract's evaluation (line sum).

currency.description: ISO 4217 code copied from the contract; every amount uses it.

fx_rate_used.description:
FX conversion snapshot (ADR 0002 lock moment: invoice issue) —
locked once at the issue leg when currency ≠ org base; immutable
afterwards. `base_total_minor` is the issue-time base equivalent.

number.description: Human invoice number, unique per org (e.g. "INV-000042").

period_from.description:
The billed period, when the contract type has one (recurring /
retainer / T&M window slice); `None` for fixed-fee schedules.

po_number.description:
Client purchase-order reference (Wave 39 F): copied from the
producing contract at run time so the document carries what the
client's AP system matches against. TAX STAYS OUT by design —
the 0036 boundary stands (tax is an accounting-export concern).

run_id.description: The run that created this invoice (`None` for future manual invoices).

total_minor.description: Sum of line amounts, minor units.

ticket_number.description: The ticket's human number and title. Present so the ledger can name it.

InvoiceDetail.description: The invoice aggregate: document, lines, and payment receipts.

InvoiceLine.description:
One persisted billing line; mirrors the engine's `BillingCandidateLine`
(kind reuse via [`crate::entities::BillingLineKind`]) minus the
denormalized contract/client names.

fx_rate_used.description:
FX conversion snapshot (ADR 0002 lock moment: time-entry costing —
the run pricing labor into this line) when currency ≠ org base.

quantity_minutes.description: Labor minutes on the line (T&M / overage); 0 for amount lines.

InvoiceMutationResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for invoice mutations.

InvoicePayment.description:
A payment receipt recorded through the `PaymentProvider` seam. The
provider stays a string (`none` in v1 — the built-in provider approves
locally without external PSP calls).

fx_rate_used.description:
FX conversion snapshot (ADR 0002 lock moment: payment settlement) —
locked once at receipt when currency ≠ org base; immutable after.

InvoiceRun.description:
The invoice-run batch record: one evaluation sweep over a window and
the roll-up of the invoices it created.

currency.description:
Currency of the summed total; `None` when the run created no
invoices (mixed currencies are rejected before any write).

number.description: Human run number, unique per org (e.g. "RUN-000007").

InvoiceRunResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for an invoice run.

InvoiceRunSignoff.description:
The reviewer sign-off recorded per invoice run (Wave 39 V8): the
close checklist a human attested before the run fired. One row per
run; the run-create seam refuses an unsigned run.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code — required for free-standing credits; when
`invoice_id` is set it must match the invoice's currency.

invoice_id.description:
The invoice the credit is raised against (issuing context). When
set, the credit's currency is the invoice's.

agreement_ref.description: Free-form contract/agreement reference when no contract row exists.

contract_id.description: Agreement anchor where a contract row exists.

is_lease.description:
When true the lease terms below are required and stamp the issued
asset's 0061 rental fields.

IssuedInvoice.description: One issued invoice: the document plus its lines.

user_id.description:
Whose journey; defaults to the caller (another user requires
owner/admin).

oneOf.description: The dispatcher's explicit row, when one exists.

The start point travel estimates will run from (explicit row when
set, else the auto-suggestion).

travel_minutes.description: Booked travel minutes into this stop (the appointment field).

category_id.description: Survives category deletion (the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL).

client_visible.description: The article half of the client-facing gate (portal v2 honors it).

content_jsonb.description:
Canonical rich content (ADR 0007): the versioned envelope
`{"schema_ver": 1, "doc": <tiptap>}` — `None` for legacy rows the
0077 backfill has not seen (reads fall back to `body`).

KbArticleStatus.description:
Article lifecycle. Closed vocabulary so filtering and the client-facing
rule stay deterministic: `draft` (staff authoring), `published`
(readable, searchable), `archived` (retired, out of the active tree —
content edits are refused while archived; unarchive to edit).

KbCategory.description: A KB category: grouping + ordering for the article tree.

client_visible.description:
The category half of the client-facing gate: an article is visible
to portal clients only when this AND the article flag are set (and
the article is published).

slug.description:
Stable per-org handle (unique); portals and imports reference this,
never the row id.

KbEmbed.description:
One embed instance attached to a KB article. Its sanction source is
the registry row resolved at write time (`provider_slug` snapshots the
handle; `provider_id` clears when the provider row is deleted, which
renders the embed as blocked until re-resolved).

KbEmbedProvider.description:
An oEmbed allowlist entry. `org_id` is `None` for the platform-shipped
system rows (`is_system`, immutable from the API); org rows are the
admin-managed registry extensions.

host_patterns.description: Exact host names this provider accepts.

oembed_endpoint.description:
oEmbed endpoint template; `{url}` is substituted once, and the
substituted value is always percent-encoded before the fetch.

slug.description: Stable per-org handle (unique; system rows use the same space).

url_regex.description:
Regex over the resource URL (Rust regex syntax); validated at
write time by the caller.

KbExternalDocument.description:
A linked external document (KB2): a SharePoint/OneDrive/Drive URL with
title, permission note, and the last link-check result. `article_id`
attaches it to an article — client-facing exposure rides that
article's client-visible gate; standalone rows are staff-only.

ready.description: True when every member has enough in-stock units at the location.

width_mm.description: Band width: the FULL content width (the QR sits above it, never over it).

LabelEntityView.description: Which entity a rendered label names.

deep_link.description:
The canonical deep link — the QR payload, and what `POST
/api/scan/resolve` hands back for the printed label.

font_mm.description:
The effective font size for this line: `0.72 × height_mm` when the
text fits, shrunk (floor `0.45 × height_mm`) until it does. The ZPL
`^A0N` height and the browser preview both use THIS number, so the
print and the preview can never disagree on how big the text is.

truncated.description:
True when even the smallest font could not fit the text and the tail
was cut — surfaced in the UI, never silent.

LabelRenderResponse.description:
The rendered label: geometry in millimetres, the QR and Code128 as
inline SVG markup (render them as images — never as script), and
optionally the exact ZPL the desktop shell sends to a Zebra printer.

sample.description: True when deterministic sample values were rendered (designer preview).

LabelTemplateView.description:
The template as the API exposes it; `width_mm`/`height_mm` are the
resolved physical size (preset or custom), so clients never re-derive it.

at_pct.description: Fires when consumed budget reaches this percent (1..=500).

LayoutField.description:
One field in a layout's schema. The `fields` column stores an array of
these (as JSON); the API validates document `fields` objects against
them.

type.description: text | number | date | bool | select | url | email

LinkCheckResponse.description: The link-check response: the refreshed row plus the outcome.

LinkCheckStatus.description:
Outcome of a link-check. `unreachable` covers DNS/TLS/HTTP failures —
the record exists but could not be verified.

LinkKind.description:
Either endpoint of a link. Documents, passwords, assets, and secret
records can link FROM; documents, passwords, clients, tickets, KB
articles, assets, and secret records can be linked TO (asset kind
added in migration 0054; secret kind added in migration 0078 — the
native vault joins the cross-entity RecordLink seam, ADR 0006).

semantic_class.description:
CI6 semantic class filter (workstation | server | vm |
network_appliance | printer | iot).

include_retired.description:
Include retired nodes (admin editors + the manifest want them;
pickers default to false).

LoanItemRequest.description:
One device to issue: from org stock (item + optional serial) or an
existing fleet asset.

overdue_only.description: Only open loans past their expected return.

LoginResponse.description:
Login outcome: tokens directly, or a short-lived MFA bridge token when
any second factor is enrolled. Untagged so legacy clients that ignore
`mfa_required` keep parsing the plain token pair they always got.

methods.description: Second factors able to satisfy this login.

tool_call_id.description: For `tool` messages: the tool call id being answered.

tool_calls.description:
For `assistant` messages that requested tools: the provider-wire
tool_calls round-trip.

MaintenanceWindow.description:
Planned downtime: an absolute UTC interval during which SLA clocks do
not consume business-time budget (vendor maintenance, change freezes).

ManifestApiKey.description:
API-key metadata. `key_hash` (the credential verifier) and the raw key
material are structurally absent — only the display prefix survives.

board_id.description: Board the rule is scoped to; null = every board in the org.

subject_kind.description:
What the rule's subject is: `ticket` (the historical default) or
`board` — a rule that fires on ticket-less envelopes (Wave 43
lane 3). Absent from a pre-lane manifest, so it defaults.

trigger_event.description: Domain event type from the envelope, e.g. `ticket.created`.

require_checklist_close.description: Pre-close checklist enforcement toggle (workflow discipline flag).

statuses.description:
Custom statuses; ALWAYS one per semantic category (defaults-first
seeding guarantees category coverage, never removed by edits).

transitions.description:
Explicit transition adjacency between this board's statuses. Empty
means the semantic-category floor applies (any→any except identity
and closed→open), not "no transitions".

ManifestBoardStatus.description:
One custom status, bound to its semantic category. Renames and colors
never change behavior — consumers must branch on `category`, not `name`.

category.description:
Semantic category: open | in_progress | waiting | closed. THE
binding every SLA/automation/reporting behavior keys on.

is_entry.description: Tickets may enter this status directly at creation.

client_name.description: Stable semantic sort key (ids only break ties across re-imports).

value.description:
The typed payload (uuid string for reference kinds, boolean for
toggles); `null` when `disabled`.

ManifestCustomField.description:
One custom field definition. `config` is the kind-specific document
(select options, validation bounds, …) exactly as stored.

archived_at.description:
Present when the definition was archived (still a customization the
preflight must see; the values it shaped may still exist).

entity.description: Entity the field attaches to: ticket | client | contact | asset.

kind.description: Field kind: text | number | date | select | multiselect | bool | url | user.

at_pct.description: Percent of the target's business-time budget consumed at firing.

notify_user_ids.description: JSON array of user ids to notify.

ManifestReportDefinition.description:
One stored report definition (TASKLIST R3). The spec body rides as its
stored jsonb document (`{filters, group_by, measures}`) exactly like
custom-field `config` — the registry-validated view/viz slugs travel as
their own fields so a preflight can flag deprecated constructs without
re-deriving validation. Nothing here is secret-bearing: definitions
reference the read-model catalog only, never credentials or data.

scope.description:
Visibility scope: `org` (published org-wide) or `self` (private to
the creator; admins see all). Preflight-relevant because org-scope
definitions are shared surface, self-scope ones are personal.

spec.description: Spec body document: `{filters, group_by, measures}` as stored.

ManifestRole.description: One org-owned role row of the manifest (a custom role or a forked copy).

builtin.description: Shipped preset tag, `null` for org-created roles.

forked_from.description: Fork origin preset tag, `null` unless the row is a forked copy.

permissions.description:
The full matrix vocabulary (`{"matrix": {"module", "action"}}`
entries plus bare special strings) — verbatim for the preflight.

ManifestSections.description:
Section container. All fields are always present; empty org state is an
empty array, never an absent key. New sections append here.

api_keys.description: API-key metadata minus secret material (no hashes, no raw keys).

boards.description:
Per-board workflow: the board identity plus its statuses (each bound
to a semantic category — the defaults-first guarantee) and its
explicit transition adjacency. An EMPTY transitions array means the
semantic-category floor applies, not "no transitions".

client_workflow_overrides.description:
Per-client workflow overrides (Wave 12 lane 5): every client-scoped
override of the org workflow defaults, rows verbatim. The override
registry (`core_domain::workflow_overrides`) is the closed key set;
the preflight must see which constructs each client's rows reference
so a migration touching those constructs transforms the rows in the
same transaction (§4.5).

custom_fields.description:
Custom field definitions across all entities (tickets, clients,
contacts, assets), including archived ones.

report_definitions.description:
Stored report definitions (TASKLIST R3): registry-validated specs
over the versioned read-model views. Covered so the upgrade
preflight (U6) can flag any definition whose `kind`/spec columns
reference deprecated view or column constructs (policy §5).

roles.description:
Role rows (Wave 13 lane 6, RB1 — ADR 0004: role rows are
customizations-as-data covered by U5/U6 like any other section).
This section is the ORG-OWNED rows only: custom roles and forked
copies (including forked presets with their origin tag). Shipped
preset rows are default state, not customization — they stay
canonical and restorable, so the preflight sees no drift.

settings.description:
Org-scope settings-registry overrides (user-scope rows are per-user
preferences, not org customization).

sla.description: SLA configuration: calendars and policies with escalation ladders.

taxonomy.description:
Ticket type/category/subcategory trees (Wave 11 lane 3).
Classification-only (§5): exported so the preflight sees the full
classification surface; retired rows INCLUDED (tickets may still
reference them). Categories are flat — `parent_id` reconstructs
the exactly-two-level tree.

webhooks.description: Webhook subscriptions with event-type filters, never secrets.

ManifestSlaCalendar.description: One named SLA calendar row with its flattened business calendar body.

calendar.description: Timezone / weekday windows / holidays / maintenance document.

ManifestSlaPolicy.description:
One SLA policy with its targets document, embedded fallback calendar,
calendar attachment, and escalation ladder.

calendar.description: Embedded fallback calendar; governs while `calendar_id` is null.

calendar_id.description: Attached named calendar; null keeps the embedded one authoritative.

targets.description: Targets document keyed by priority string.

ManifestTaxonomy.description: The two classification trees of one org.

ManifestTaxonomyCategory.description: One category (root when `parent_id` is null) or subcategory.

ManifestTransition.description: One allowed status change, `from` → `to`, both ids from the SAME board.

ManifestWebhook.description:
One webhook subscription. The HMAC signing secret is structurally
absent: it exists only at creation time and in the sealed column.

event_types.description: Event-type filter; empty array = wildcard (all event types).

marked.description: Rows flipped from unread to read (idempotent under retry).

MatchCandidate.description:
One technician candidate for one ticket: the skills this candidate is
missing (an empty list = fully qualified right now).

MatchQuery.description: GET /api/dispatch/match query: how many unassigned tickets to match.

MeetingAssigneeScope.description:
Who a meeting type books against: ONE user's calendar, or the
unioned availability of a free-form admin-defined group.

MeetingType.description:
A bookable template: duration, buffer before/after, booking window,
org-editable free-form `parameters`, and the assignee scope. Auto-
email is per-template; with transport `none` the send is skipped.

parameters.description:
Free-form org-edited payload (location hint, agenda, questions…).
Consumers must tolerate any shape; nothing in behavior keys off it.
Free-form org-edited payload (location hint, agenda, questions…).

auto_merge_threshold.description:
The org's auto-merge threshold — surfaced inline so the reviewer
sees WHY this row was queued instead of auto-merged.

fields.description:
The field-by-field picker's rows: the union of both sides'
observed/curated keys with per-side provenance.

related_pending.description:
The queued candidates this merge would ride along with (other
pending candidates sharing either side) so batch context is visible.

mfa_token.description: The `mfa_token` from POST /api/auth/login when mfa_required was set.

trust_device.description:
"Trust this computer": keep this browser signed in for
`TRUSTED_DEVICE_TTL_SECS` instead of the default refresh window.

`#[serde(default)]` so every existing client keeps working unchanged —
an absent field means "do not trust", which is the conservative answer
and the one a caller that never heard of the option should get.

allOf.description: Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + version.

reset_sla.description:
Default false: the existing SLA clock state is PRESERVED verbatim
(board membership is classification, not a lifecycle event). true =
re-initialize the clocks under the org's default policy anchored at
the move moment.

status_id.description:
Pin the target status explicitly (the retry path after a
`board_move_status_conflict`). Must be a status of the target
board; omitted = remap through the semantic categories.

MoveSpec.description: One move in a batch: the booking's new user and slot.

MovementMutationResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response for ledger legs.

MutationMeta.description:
Read-your-write metadata every mutation response carries (IF2), merged
as the additive `mutation` object alongside the entity fields.

before.description:
Prior entity snapshot (the undo substrate). `null` on creates. The
OpenAPI schema stays a plain object; generated clients get the
runtime-typed view through the SDK's `snapshotOf` accessor.

idempotency_key.description:
The idempotency key that claimed this result, when the caller
supplied one.

seq.description:
Monotonic per-entity sequence: strictly increases by one per
applied write, so clients order reconciliations against the event
stream.

version.description:
Version token for If-Match-style writes; mirrors `seq`. Echo it in
the next write's `version` field.

MutationParams.description:
The autosave mutation parameters every gated create/update body carries
(flattened into the request struct — purely additive fields).

idempotency_key.description:
Idempotency key: the same key with the same payload replays the
SAME stored result (never double-applies); the same key with a
different payload is a typed 409. Generate one per user edit
debounce/retry episode (UUID works).

version.description:
If-Match-style version: the entity `version` the caller last saw
(the `mutation.version` of the previous response). A mismatch
rejects the write with a typed 409 `version_conflict` carrying
`expected`/`provided`; omit for creates and for legacy callers.

MyWorkItem.description:
One cross-board my-work queue row (TASKLIST 2.11): the ticket plus the
annotations the Today screen renders per the mockup.

board_id.description: The source board of this cross-board row.

client_name.description: Client short label for the squared tag (`None` = internal ticket).

due_at.description: Manual deadline set on the ticket itself.

sla_resolution_due.description:
SLA resolution deadline when state exists; the UI prefers this over
`due_at` for the right-aligned countdown column.

NodeAudience.description:
Who a node is for. Decides palette visibility against the LLM tool
catalogue — a power user and the authoring model should not see the
same list. A plugin entry that declares nothing stays `human` until it
says otherwise (an undeclared node never auto-joins the model's view).

NodeCatalogueView.description:
The catalogue read: version, digest, and the nodes the caller asked
for. The version and digest let a saved document say which release it
was validated against, and make two builds claiming the same release
with different declarations detectable.

NodeFamily.description:
Which part of the workflow surface a node belongs to. The palette groups
by family; the properties panel and the LLM tool catalogue both filter
on it.

NodeTier.description:
The catalogue's three tiers (docs/reference/workflow-node-catalogue.md).
Tier A is always visible and first in search; Tier B is the domain long
tail reached through the generic operation nodes; Tier C is
plugin-contributed.

NodeView.description:
One node as the web and the SDK consume it. Schemas ride as JSON so a
properties panel renders from them directly instead of hand-writing a
form per node.

emits.description:
The event types this node can produce, the seam the static loop
refusal reads.

executor.description:
The executor path this node rides: a closed domain operation for a
Tier A wrapper, the generic path for Tier B, the plugin surface
kind for Tier C.

idempotency_key.description:
The autosave claim key — the composer must echo it back on submit
so the committed comment clears this exact draft row.

oneOf.description: The caller's draft (per user × ticket); null when none is saved.

NotificationPage.description: One page of the inbox plus the cursor to continue with.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next request; `None` means exhausted.

error.description:
The operator may decline; the vendor then redirects with an error
and no code. That is a user choice, not a failure, so it gets its own
message instead of "invalid code".

message.description:
Set only on a DECLINED consent, so the UI can say "you cancelled"
rather than showing a generic failure.

OAuthStartResponse.description: Where the operator lands after consent.

authorize_url.description:
The vendor consent URL. The operator is redirected here; the callback
URL is pre-registered by the operator with their OAuth client.

OidcPresetInfo.description: One entry of the declarative first-party preset catalog.

redirect_guidance.description: Where to register the redirect URI on the provider side.

name.description: URL path segment used by login/link routes.

preset.description: Declarative preset this provider was created from, when any.

OnCallBlock.description: An absolute UTC on-call rotation segment for one user.

low_only.description: true → only rows at/below the reorder point.

OnHandRow.description: The stock-on-hand read model row (`qty leaking thresholds`).

low.description: The instant-first low flag the UI + automations key on.

unresolved.description: Live: the member still has unresolved steps (drives re-trigger UX).

legacy_wizard_completed.description:
Legacy fallback: true while NO per-step flags exist yet but the old
flat key did (U6-safe supersede).

dismissed.description: "never show this again" was recorded for this step.

satisfied.description: Server-verified live gate state right now.

user_id.description:
The member whose first-run flow is re-triggered (admin calls);
omitted means re-run the CALLER's own user onboarding.

OrgBillingPreview.description:
Org-wide preview: every billable contract's evaluation for the window
plus the grand total — the shape a Wave-9 invoice run will consume.

total_minor.description: Sum over evaluations, minor units (mixed currencies reject).

base_currency.description: The org's ONE base (reporting) currency (ADR 0002, FX1).

OrgQuotaView.description:
One metric beside its configured limit, if any, and the percentage of
it in use.

limits_configured.description:
Whether the org configured ANY limit. `false` means every
`percent` below is `None` because there is nothing to measure
against — the answer for an unconfigured org, not a default.

metrics.description:
Every reportable metric in a stable order, whether or not a limit
is configured for it.

refreshed_at.description:
When the usage figures were computed. `None` while the org's row has
never been refreshed. Note that `UsageMetric::AutomationRuns` and
`WebhookDeliveries` read their all-time totals from this row, so the
totals are as of this instant rather than as of the request.

allOf.description: Instant-first mutation parameters (IF1).

already_mapped.description: Whether the vendor org was ALREADY mapped (idempotent no-op).

OrgUsageView.description: The org's current usage, one field per recorded metric.

active_users.description:
Staff accounts that can still sign in. A disabled account is not
using anything, so it is not counted here.

audit_events_24h.description:
Audit events within `[refreshed_at - 24h, refreshed_at]` — the closest
honest per-org proxy for API activity the core records. NOT an
API-call count: reads are not audited and writes are audited
best-effort, so this counts the mutations the core chose to record,
not the requests that arrived. The window is closed at refresh time,
as with the other `_24h` fields.

automation_runs.description:
Ledgered automation execution attempts since the org's first run.
This is an ALL-TIME total, so it does not carry the staleness rule
the `_24h` fields do — but it is still only as current as
`refreshed_at`, since the row is written once per refresh.

automation_runs_24h.description:
Ledgered automation execution attempts within
`[refreshed_at - 24h, refreshed_at]`. The window is CLOSED at
refresh time, so it ages with the row rather than sliding to the
moment of the read; compare against `refreshed_at` before treating
this as current.

managed_devices.description:
Active managed client devices. This is an ACTIVE-INVENTORY count:
`device_assets` has no connectivity or last-seen signal, so it cannot
measure "connected" clients. Status is connector-compatibility free
text matched case-insensitively, so orgs whose connectors store a
different status string under-report — this is a floor, not a census.

object_store_bytes.description:
Recorded object-store payload bytes (a floor; see the method note in
migration 0131 — staged import chunks record no size).

refreshed_at.description:
When these numbers were computed (the materialized row's own
timestamp). `None` while the refresh sweep has not reached the org
yet, which is exactly when the counts should not be trusted. Every
`_24h` field below is a window that ENDS at this instant; as the row
ages, so does the window, so read this before trusting those fields.

tickets_by_category.description:
Tickets per workflow category (the closed vocabulary). Category,
not board status name: names are per-board and repeat across boards,
so a name-keyed map would collapse distinct statuses.

tickets_total.description:
Tickets across every category — the total an inventory limit
constrains.

unavailable.description:
Metrics this build cannot compute honestly, each with the reason.
Empty is not possible today; the list exists so a monitoring
surface can render the gap rather than silently miss a column.

webhook_deliveries.description:
Ledgered webhook delivery attempts since the org's first. One row per
ATTEMPT, so a retried delivery counts three times. All-time, so no
window rule — only the row's own `refreshed_at` currency.

webhook_deliveries_24h.description:
Ledgered webhook delivery attempts within
`[refreshed_at - 24h, refreshed_at]` — the same CLOSED,
refresh-time-frozen window as `automation_runs_24h`.

OrgUser.description:
Directory view of one staff user (route-level DTO; `org_role` is the
user's highest-precedence builtin role, `null` for custom-only).

oneOf.description: Present on invite only: the setup token for the invitee.

OrgUserMutationResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response (IF2): the invited (still inactive)
user at the top level plus the one-time setup token and the additive
`mutation` metadata.

org_greeting.description:
The org's own greeting — what opens mail the workspace sends to its
staff, and the fallback for a member with none (Wave 42).

ready.description:
Whether the SELECTED transport has a usable credential/endpoint
combination (the honest not-configured bit the UI renders).

ses_region.description:
The SES region this org sends through, when one is set. Plain config,
never a secret — the admin UI shows it so an operator can see which
data centre is in play.

signature_policy.description:
`allowed` | `org_locked`: whether members may sign with their own
details. The UI renders a locked org's state rather than a disabled
field with no reason.

OverrideDeclarationView.description: One registry declaration, projected for the settings/admin surface.

org_default_setting.description: The settings-registry key carrying the org default for toggles.

OverrideEntry.description:
One resolved override entry: the declaration it validated against, the
resolution outcome, which layer supplied it, the raw org default and client
row, the renderable detail, and any resolution issues (e.g. a stale
cross-board status override that fell back to the board's entry status).

issues.description: Typed drift/validation notes (never empty on a fallback).

org_default.description: The org default this resolution inherited from, when one existed.

source.description: Which layer supplied the effective value.

OverrideValueKind.description:
The value shapes a client override accepts. The wire value is the plain
JSON payload (uuid string / boolean); the kind exists so validation can
reject a mistyped payload before persistence.

user_id.description: Owner of the row being deleted (must match self-or-admin rule).

PasswordEntry.description:
A vault credential. `secret_ciphertext` is AES-256-GCM from
core-api crypto::seal — plaintext NEVER reaches the database layer,
and this entity never carries it either (reveal is a dedicated,
audited endpoint response type).

last_rotated_at.description: Stamped by the same update that moves `rotate_at` forward.

rotate_at.description:
Operator-scheduled rotation due date (Wave 19 lane 3); the worker
sweep reminds once past it (durable at-most-once marker on the
row in the DB; the entities carry no sweep housekeeping).

PasswordHistoryEntry.description: One archived secret ciphertext from a credential's change history.

PasswordReveal.description:
The audited reveal response: plaintext is returned exactly once,
over TLS, to a caller holding `passwords:edit`; the reveal emits a
`password.revealed` contract event (provenance query: "who looked
at this credential and when").

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

event_type.description:
Promote/demote a source between alert and generic M2M profiles.
`Some(None)` reverts to alert-source; `Some(Some(v))` sets the
emitted event type.

payload_schema_ref.description: Set/clear the payload contract pin the same way.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key +
If-Match `version`. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

blocks.description: When present, replaces the whole prepaid-block set.

caps.description: When present, replaces the whole cap set.

clear_minimum.description:
Explicit clear for the minimum commitment: PATCH cannot
distinguish "absent" from "null" on the flat field, so removing
a minimum sends `clear_minimum: true`.

oneOf.description: When present, sets the escalator; `clear_escalator: true` removes it.

fees.description: When present, replaces the whole fee schedule.

minimum_commitment_minor.description: When present, sets/clears the minimum commitment (`None` clears).

rates.description: When present, replaces the whole rate card.

base_currency.description:
Present + different ⇒ a governed base-currency change (ADR 0002):
refused with a typed conflict while conversion snapshots exist.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

budget_minor.description:
Wave 39 lane 4: tri-state budget/fee updates on the phase's
billing record (`Some(Some(v))` sets, `Some(None)` clears,
`None` = no change; `clear_*` drops the whole record when both
fields would be empty).

start_date.description:
Tri-state, matching the budget fields below: `Some(Some(d))` sets a
date, `Some(None)` takes the phase off the Gantt, and an absent field
leaves it alone. Without the distinction, renaming a phase would
quietly erase its planned window.

oneOf.description: `disabled` blocks login AND every authenticated request immediately.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

billing_contract_id.description:
`Some(Some(v))` links the contract; `Some(None)` unlinks;
`None` = no change (Wave 39 lane 4, report P2).

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

oneOf.description:
Lifecycle moves other than completion (pending / in_progress /
blocked / cancelled). Reaching `completed` MUST go through the
complete endpoint so dependency gating + billing events cannot be
skipped.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + entity
version. Absent in legacy clients — purely additive.

custom_fields.description:
Custom-field values to upsert. Partial semantics: only listed fields
change, each validated against its definition.

type_id.description:
Classification (Wave 11 lane 3): `"type_id": null` clears,
an id sets (the node must exist in this org and not be retired),
an absent member leaves it untouched. Purely descriptive: behavior
binds to the semantic categories, never these trees.

PatchTravelDraftRequest.description:
PATCH /api/dispatch/travel-drafts/{id} body — every member optional;
absent members are left untouched.

reason.description: Optional reason, preserved on the segment forever.

session_id.description: Omit to act on the caller's active timer.

PaymentMutationResponse.description:
Payment receipt response. The invoice is nested (not flattened) so
the stored replay payload — `{payment, invoice}` plus the merged
mutation metadata — deserializes into this shape byte-identically.

PhaseAllocationListView.description: Every allocation in the org, or in one project.

share_percent.description:
1..=100, CHECK-enforced in the database. A 0 or a 150 entering the
forecast would corrupt every capacity number on the page, so the
bound is enforced in the schema rather than only in this handler.

PhaseAllocationView.description: One stated allocation of a technician to a project phase.

PhaseBurn.description:
The burn read model for one phase: consumed minutes priced against the
project's linked contract versus the contracted budget, with a typed
alert state (report P3). Amounts are in the budget's currency.

alert.description: Typed alert: `none` under budget, `warn` past 80%, `over` past 100%.

budget_minor.description: The contracted budget (minor units); `None` = unbudgeted phase.

consumed_minor.description:
Consumed value in minor units (unit_amount_minor per-line pricing
folded up; 0 when the phase carries a pure fee).

consumed_minutes.description: Consumed minutes (approved billable entries scoped to the phase).

PhaseBurnAlert.description:
The phase-burn alert state. `warn` fires at ≥80% consumed; `over` at
≥100%. Never silent: the read model carries the label, the UI renders it.

PhaseGanttView.description: One phase as the Gantt draws it, with its budget burn attached.

burn_alert.description:
`none` under budget, `warn` at/over 80%, `over` at/over 100%.
`None` for an unbudgeted phase, because "no budget" is not "under
budget" and rendering it green would be a false reassurance.

planned_days.description: Planned days, inclusive of both ends. `None` when undated.

PipelineDeal.description: An opportunity: one client, optionally one quote, one current stage.

closed_at.description: Set when the deal lands on a won/lost stage.

PipelineDealTransition.description:
One immutable stage move (or the initial placement, with a NULL
`from_stage_id`). Appended in the same transaction as the move.

PipelineStage.description: One ordered stage of the org's pipeline.

PluginCapability.description:
The CLOSED capability vocabulary a v2 manifest may declare and an
install may be granted. Capabilities are declarative names that map
onto the EXISTING permission matrix — a grant never creates a new
permission, it resolves to a standard [`Permission`] and every check
flows through `core_domain::policy` like any human actor's. There is
deliberately NO admin capability: `special:manage_plugins`, user
management, billing, and audit-log specials are human-only grants a
plugin can never hold (deny-by-default — the vocabulary simply has
no key for them).

PluginInstallStatus.description:
Install lifecycle. Deny-by-default: `Disabled` until an explicit
admin enable; `Revoked` is terminal (registry revocation or explicit
revoke) — a revoked install never runs again until re-installed.

PluginManifestBody.description:
The declarative manifest as submitted. `interface_version` is
server-pinned (the runtime speaks exactly one version), so a caller
cannot publish an entry the runtime would refuse.

oneOf.description:
ADR 0009 §6 — which runtime the published artifact speaks. Absent
⇒ `wasm`, byte-identical to every request body published before
Wave 43 lane 4. Without this field the route FORCED wasm: a
connector's `connector_profile` is refused on a wasm manifest, so
`POST /api/plugins/catalog` could never publish the artifact kind
Wave 43 lane 4's outbound seeding actually needs. `validate()` is
called on the built manifest, so an incoherent combination is
still rejected here rather than at install time.

ADR 0009 §6 full semantics (Wave 19 lane 2) — the modeled
connector governance profile (webhook endpoints + scopes).
Valid only on http_connector manifests; wasm manifests refuse it.

settings_schema.description: ADR 0009 §4 — optional JSON-Schema for manifest-rendered settings.

oneOf.description:
§4.6 (Wave 34 lane 4, amended per kind by ADR 0017 §3 in Wave 43
lane 4) — the declarative surface profile. On a wasm manifest every
section is available; on an http_connector the three UI sections
refuse and the three executor sections
(automation_action / automation_trigger / read) are allowed.

PluginManifestV2.description:
The declarative v2 plugin manifest: name/version/capabilities — a
DATA document describing what a plugin IS and what it may ask for.
It is never executable content: the runtime executes nothing from a
manifest, and "install" only ever adopts a catalog entry's manifest
snapshot.

oneOf.description:
ADR 0009 §6 — the artifact GOVERNANCE profile the manifest
declares: WASM executables and HTTP connectors ship in one
lifecycle track but distinct tabs. Absent ⇒ `wasm` (the
declarative manifest/permission baseline every v1 manifest was
published as); connectors must DECLARE the kind. Additive to the
v2 shape; unknown keys reject at deserialization (closed
vocabulary).

capabilities.description:
The capabilities the plugin MAY be granted. Grants at install
time are a subset of this list — a grant outside the manifest's
declared set is rejected.

oneOf.description:
ADR 0009 §6 full semantics (Wave 19 lane 2) — the connector
governance profile: webhook endpoints + outbound scopes as MODELED
manifest fields, never free text. Valid and OPTIONAL ONLY on
`http_connector` manifests (a connector may legitimately declare no
webhooks — the default posture an absent profile already encodes);
forbidden on `wasm` manifests. Declared endpoints are the
connector's egress-allowlist seed (the same posture the WASM
resource profile carries); declared scopes render on the consent
screen verbatim so an admin consents to exactly the SaaS scopes the
connector asks for.

interface_version.description:
The interface version this manifest was written against; must
equal [`PLUGIN_RUNTIME_INTERFACE_VERSION`] or the runtime refuses
the entry.

settings_schema.description:
ADR 0009 §4 — the optional JSON-Schema the manifest declares for
its per-install settings. The Plugins surface renders config FROM
this schema (typed-registry doctrine: no hand-authored
per-plugin pages); a manifest with no schema gets
consent/enable/disable only. Additive to the v2 shape.

oneOf.description:
Wave 34 lane 4 (§4.6) — the declarative UI-surface profile:
widgets, automation action kinds, report render kinds, custom-field
validators, trigger sources, and read nodes.

The rule is PER KIND (ADR 0017 §3, Wave 43 lane 4). On a `wasm`
manifest every section is available. On an `http_connector` the
three UI sections (`widget`, `report_render`, `field_validator`)
refuse — a connector has no in-product UI surface to govern — while
the three EXECUTOR sections (`automation_action`,
`automation_trigger`, `read`) are allowed, because a connector
already holds credentials and network egress and a sandbox does
not. Optional on both: an EMPTY profile carries no consent weight.
Consent renders the declarations verbatim, and each section only
registers when its capability (`ui.widgets` /
`automation.actions` / `reports.render` / `fields.validate` /
`automation.triggers` / `automation.reads`) is granted. Additive to
the v2 shape.

declared_triggers.description:
The event types the org's plugins declare as triggers. They belong
to the trigger catalogue, not to this list, because a plugin
trigger arrives through the signed ingest and needs no surface
node at all.

PluginNodeView.description:
One plugin-contributed node as the palette and the picker consume it.
Only live entries are listed — a revoked install's rows are gone, not
present-and-broken — and the entry carries its install so the canvas
can say whose node it is.

kind.description:
`action`, `read` or `trigger`. A `trigger` is an EVENT TYPE the
connector declares through the signed ingest, not a node — the
trigger catalogue makes it subscribable.

PluginPublisherRevoked.description:
`plugin.publisher_revoked` — the org-side vouch was withdrawn;
the badge disappears and history is preserved.

PluginPublisherVerification.description:
Marketplace v2 verified-publisher registry row (Wave 22). A
publisher is a NORMALIZED SOURCE IDENTITY; verification is per-org
(this org vouches this publisher), admin-curated, and additive over
the v1 distribution formats.

PluginPublisherVerified.description:
`plugin.publisher_verified` — Marketplace v2: an owner/admin vouched
for a publisher identity on behalf of the org (per-org badge, never
global). Additive over the v1 distribution surfaces.

PluginRating.description:
Marketplace v2 per-user rating on one artifact RELEASE (the
`{source_kind, source_url, artifact_digest}` triple). One rating per
user per release; re-rating is an upsert.

artifact_digest.description: sha256 hex of the artifact release.

PluginRatingRecorded.description:
`plugin.rating_recorded` — Marketplace v2 social layer: one staff
member's 1–5 star rating on an artifact release (upsert semantics —
a re-rate wins and the event fires once per upsert).

PluginRuntimeKind.description:
The plugin-side artifact vocabulary for the roster tabs (WASM vs HTTP
connector). Skills are NOT in this closed set — the skill half lives
on `PluginArtifactKind::Skill` in the distribution seam (0079). Parse
is strict: a manifest naming an ungovernable kind cannot exist.

PluginSettingsUpdated.description:
`plugin.settings_updated` — a per-install config rendered FROM the
pinned manifest's settings JSON-Schema changed (validated at the
write boundary; no hand-authored per-plugin settings pages exist).

config_keys.description:
The validated config keys (values stay server-side; consumers
refetch through the settings surface).

PluginSourceKind.description:
The closed source vocabulary — every distribution adapter records the
same provenance chain, typed by the kind of source it is.

PluginStagedImportApproved.description:
`plugin.staged_import_approved` — an owner/admin reviewed the consent
diff and the wait ended in adoption: the catalog entry/version +
install were minted (plugins) or the agent skill was imported
(skills), provenance recorded, still deny-by-default on enable.

PluginStagedImportCreated.description:
`plugin.staged_import_created` — a member upload (skill or plugin)
landed staged: validated, never executed, visible only to its
uploader and admins. Capabilities are the staged manifest's DECLARED
keys; consent happens at approval, never here.

PluginStagedImportRefused.description:
`plugin.staged_import_refused` — the reviewer declined the staged
import (terminal for that row; the uploader may re-stage fresh).

PluginSurfaceProfile.description:
Wave 34 lane 4 (§4.6): the modeled UI-surface profile a WASM manifest
may declare — dashboard/ticket-pane WIDGETS, automation ACTION KINDS,
report RENDER KINDS, and custom-field VALIDATORS. Everything here is
DECLARATIVE: closed render/effect vocabularies plus JSON-Schema
subsets the core validates and executes. A plugin ships declarations,
never code the browser or the rule engine runs raw (agent-safety
§4.8).

actions.description: Automation action kinds registered alongside the built-ins.

field_validators.description: JSON-Schema validators for board custom fields.

reads.description:
Wave 43 lane 4 (ADR 0017 §3, §5): READ nodes, the only kind that
lets a workflow FETCH from an external system. Every entry carries
its own guardrails; there is no default that weakens them.

render_kinds.description: Render kinds contributed to the report builder.

triggers.description:
Wave 43 lane 4 (ADR 0017 §3): TRIGGER sources the plugin
contributes — the event type a rule can fire on. This is the half
of the `automation_action` symmetry that was missing: a plugin
could contribute an action but never a trigger.

widgets.description: Widgets the plugin registers (dashboard or ticket-pane slots).

PluginUpdatePending.description:
`plugin.update_pending` — an update proposal is waiting on the
re-consent diff: the OLD version stays pinned and running until the
owner/admin consents; consent commits the swap.

current_version.description: The version still running (pinned until consented).

PmRun.description: One append-only PM run ledger row.

PmSchedule.description:
A recurring/scheduled ticket (PM schedule): a ticket template plus the
typed cadence (same shape as report schedules). The worker claims due
rows; core-api generates the instance and advances the cadence.

config.description:
Pod id → RBAC level → visible. Absent entries fall back to the
client registry defaults.

targets.description: Targets keyed by priority ("p1".."p4"), business minutes.

uses_embedded_calendar.description: True while the policy governs itself via its embedded calendar.

PortalAppointmentRequestMutationResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for appointment-request writes.
The request fields sit at the TOP LEVEL (flattened) so the stored
replay payload (`request` serialized + merged mutation metadata)
round-trips byte-identically.

PortalAttachmentView.description: Portal attachment view: metadata only (bytes stream on download).

allOf.description: Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1).

PortalCancelRequest.description: Body for the portal cancel (idempotency parameters only).

allOf.description: Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key.

oneOf.description: `on_site | remote` (internal/personal are staff-only kinds).

user_id.description: The staff member whose calendar the client asked for.

PortalCsatView.description: Portal CSAT survey state as the in-app response route sees it.

status.description: `valid` renders the form; `responded` renders the thank-you state.

PortalInvoice.description:
The client-facing invoice document view. Deliberately NOT the staff
entity: dunning internals and staff notes never reach the portal.

score.description: FTS rank blended with trigram similarity — ordering signal only.

q.description:
Websearch query (plain words, quoted phrases, `OR`, `-`
exclusions — Postgres websearch syntax).

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key + If-Match
`version` on the invoice.

amount_minor.description:
Amount to settle, minor units; must not exceed the outstanding
balance. Currency is always the invoice's own.

payment_method.description:
PSP payment-method surface (e.g. a confirmed Stripe `pm_*` id
from the embedded payment form). None = ledger-only none-mode
settlement; required when the org resolved provider is Stripe.

PortalPayResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for a portal payment: the
receipt, the refreshed client-facing invoice, and the additive
`mutation` metadata. Stored/replayed byte-identically under the key.

PortalPaymentView.description:
A payment receipt as the portal sees it. `created_by` stays internal
(portal identities are not staff rows; the field is always NULL on
portal-recorded rows anyway).

provider.description:
`'none'` while no external PSP is connected — the receipt is a
ledger entry, not a card charge.

PortalProfile.description: The signed-in portal identity (also served by GET /api/portal/me).

PortalQuote.description:
The client-facing quote view. Deliberately NOT the staff entity: the
creator provenance and conversion seam ids stay staff-internal — the
portal sees the document, its validity, and its lifecycle state.

valid_until.description: Last day the quote can be accepted; shown honestly on the portal.

reason.description: Optional reason, recorded in the audit trail (decline-with-reason).

PortalQuoteDecisionRequest.description:
A quote decision body (approve/decline): envelope params only; the
target status is the URL. The SAME instant-first envelope the staff
lifecycle legs use.

PortalQuoteDecisionResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for a portal quote decision.

PortalQuoteDetail.description: The quote aggregate as the portal sees it: document + lines.

PortalQuoteLine.description: A client-facing quote line: description/qty/price/amount only.

quantity_milli.description: Quantity in thousandths of a unit (1.5 = 1500).

PortalRole.description:
Portal role tiers. `contact` is the default read/reply tier;
`approver` is behaviorally identical in v1 but exists so approval
grants (Stage 3 quote approval / Stage 4 optional client approvals)
can be layered on without re-provisioning identities; `it_manager`
ADDITIONALLY reads `in_house_update` notes. NO tier ever reads
`internal` notes — enforced by `notes::visible_kinds`, tested in
`policy` and `notes`.

PortalSlotInterval.description: Free intervals for one staff member over the query range.

user_id.description: Optional: narrow to one staff member.

PortalStaffSlots.description: One staff member's published free slots over the query range.

slots.description:
Sorted, internally disjoint, contiguous FREE stretches. A client
requests a slice of one; the server re-validates at request time
and again at approval.

comments.description: Only the kinds this tier may read, filtered by the domain policy.

status_id.description: The status id, so a client-side filter can group without guessing.

status_label.description: The status's own label, when the org allows clients to see it.

PortalTicketView.description:
A ticket as a CLIENT sees it (Wave 41 lane 12).

The ticket fields are flattened exactly as they were, so the portal client
keeps reading the same keys; two status fields are added. `status_label`
is `None` when the status is not client-visible, and the client shows the
category word instead — which is the whole point of the per-status switch
in Settings: it changes what a client is told, in words, without hiding
where the ticket stands.

PortalTierView.description:
One portal tier in the preset roster (RB1). Portal authorization is
deliberately NOT the staff matrix (see `core_domain::policy`) — the
tiers render here as data with their capability keys, but they are
per-contact settings, never staff `roles` rows and never forkable.

capabilities.description: Capability keys from the tier×capability matrix (`policy::portal_tier_allows`).

PortalUserStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a portal identity. `invited` = admin-provisioned, has not
logged in yet; first successful login flips to `active`. `disabled`
blocks login AND every authenticated portal request (checked per
request, never cached in the token).

PreferenceView.description:
One resolved preference row: which chain link supplied it (`user`,
`org_default`, or `builtin`), the channel toggles, and the quiet-hours
window with its timezone.

PresenceViewer.description: One presence viewer on an entity (roster + roster frames).

editing.description: True while the user is actively editing (vs. just viewing).

PresetView.description:
The canonical definition of one shipped preset (RB1): the presets stay
canonical even though every org carries its own rows — restore resets
a row to this set.

PreviewLabelRequest.description:
Draft render body (the designer preview). Same shape as create minus the
template identity: nothing is persisted.

Project.description:
A project engagement under a client (or internal when `client_id` is
`None`).

billing_contract_id.description:
The contract this project bills through (Wave 39 lane 4, report
P2): its rate card, blocks, and caps price the project's T&M work.
`None` = non-billable or not linked. The link validates in the
app layer (same client, active-or-draft contract).

budget_minor.description: Project budget in minor units; `None` = unbudgeted.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency for `budget_minor` (required when a budget is set).

ProjectBillingRelease.description:
One released milestone (report P1/P4): the durable record that a
completed milestone or fixed-fee phase released its amount to the
invoicing pipeline. `pending` rows bill on the first run that reaches
the window; the run flips them `billed` with the consuming invoice,
so a replay can never double-bill.

label.description: The milestone name at release time (frozen from the event).

ProjectGanttView.description: The project's Gantt: dated phases as bars, undated ones as list items.

dated.description: Phases with BOTH dates set, ordered by start then sort_order.

undated.description:
Phases with a missing end, in sort_order. The UI shows these in the
ordered list and says they are not on the timeline, rather than
placing them at an invented date.

window_from.description:
The union of dated windows, so the chart can scale to the plan
instead of to "today".

ProjectInstantiateResponse.description:
The instantiation result: the applied project plus the expansion
counts (clients render "created N phases, M tasks" without refetching).

ProjectMutationResponse.description:
Instant-first mutation response for the project entity (IF2): applied
snapshot at the top level plus the additive `mutation` metadata.

ProjectPhase.description:
A phase groups tasks into a delivery stage. A phase flagged
`is_milestone` is itself a billing milestone.

end_date.description:
Inclusive end date. CHECK-enforced `>= start_date` in the database,
because a bar drawn backwards reads as a rendering bug and is
actually a data problem the operator needs told about.

milestone_amount_minor.description:
Billing amount released when this milestone phase completes
(minor units; `None` = informational milestone).

start_date.description:
The phase's PLANNED window (Wave 34 claims close-out, claim 6).

Both ends are nullable and that is the honest state rather than a
compromise: most real projects have phases nobody has dated yet, and
a NOT NULL pair with a "today" default would draw a Gantt that lies
about the plan. A phase is drawn on the bar chart only when BOTH
ends are set; a half-dated phase stays in the ordered list and the
UI says which it is.

ProjectPhaseBudget.description:
A phase's billing budget and/or fixed-fee record (Wave 39 lane 4,
report P3/P4). One optional row per phase: `budget_minor` is the
contracted denominator the burn math consumes (T&M phases), and
`fee_minor` is the fixed fee a completed NON-milestone phase releases
(milestone phases carry their own amount on the phase row).

budget_minor.description: Contracted budget for the phase (minor units); `None` = unbudgeted.

fee_minor.description: Fixed fee released on phase completion (minor units); `None` = no fee.

ProjectTask.description:
A unit of project work. A task flagged `is_milestone` is a billing
milestone: completing it emits `project.milestone_completed`.

ProjectTemplate.description:
A reusable project blueprint. `spec` follows `core-projects::template`
(`TemplateSpec`, additive-only evolution); instantiation is a plain
transactional insert plan — templates are data, not code (policy §5).

ProjectView.description:
A saved task-list view: filter/group/sort spec over one project's tasks
(`project_id: None` = org-wide). The `spec` is a versioned, additive-only
JSON document validated at the route layer; unknown fields are tolerated
(policy §2 posture for declared customizations-as-data).

ProposalClassification.description: Proposal classification: who will see the change if it lands.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`.

granted_capabilities.description:
The grant set that WOULD apply post-consent (defaults to the
current grants; a widening validates against the new manifest).

version.description: Pin this catalog version as the update candidate.

ProvenanceEvent.description: One provenance entry: a single field change within one applied write.

actor_id.description: The acting user (or machine actor) id, when attributed.

actor_kind.description: Actor kind from the write-trail vocabulary (human, agent, ...).

after.description: Applied value; null when the field was removed in this write.

before.description: Prior value; null when the field is new.

idempotency_key.description:
The idempotency key that claimed the write, when the caller
supplied one.

ruleset_hash.description: Rule-set hash that governed the write, when present.

skill.description: Skill that authored the write, when present.

undo.description: True for undo reverts (IF7) riding the normal write path.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; absent when exhausted.

ProviderMutationResponse.description: Instant-first mutation response (IF2) for provider rows.

PublicLinkView.description:
What the public page needs to render the booking UI: the template's
bookable shape plus a slot preview over the booking window. The
horizon follows `booking_window_days`; intervals are computed in
server-side chunks and capped at [`MAX_PREVIEW_SLOTS`].

expires_at.description: Absolute expiry, when the tech set one.

slots.description:
Free intervals (unioned across the assignee scope) within the
bookable horizon; clients slice them into bookable choices.

slug.description:
Slug; version is derived server-side (max + 1) — append-only
history, never an in-place edit.

PullItem.description:
One exported row: internal id, stable source key when the row was ever
pushed under one, and the canonical projection (the SAME field catalog
the push side diffs against).

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor`; absent when exhausted.

cursor.description:
Opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor` (the last
row id). Absent = start of the family.

PurchaseBill.description:
The vendor bill: recorded as a draft, posted (FX-locked) into project
cost rollups.

currency.description: ISO 4217; every line cost is in this currency.

project_id.description: Cost-object hook for project cost rollups (NULL = unassigned).

PurchaseOrderLine.description: One PO line: quantity at milli precision, cost in minor units.

PurchaseOrderRollup.description:
The rolled-up money on a PO: ordered and received amounts in the PO
currency, integer minor units.

PurchaseOrderSummary.description:
One row of the order list: the order itself plus its own totals.

The order fields are flattened, so this is the order's old wire shape plus
a `totals` key — a client that ignores the new key keeps working, and one
that reads it stops needing a request per order to know what an order is
worth. `totals` is `null` for a caller without `ViewFinancials`, which is
the same gate the detail endpoint's totals obey: the list never leaks money
the detail page would hide.

PurchaseReceipt.description: One receipt document: goods that landed at a location against a PO.

PurchaseReceiptLine.description: One receipt line: what moved, and the ledger row it posted.

movement_id.description: The lane-1 append-only ledger row this line posted.

PurchaseReceiptView.description:
A receipt document with its traceability lines (each stamps the
lane-1 ledger `movement_id` it posted).

PushCheckpoint.description:
The checkpoint cursor of a push session: what the server has committed
and what it expects next. `last_committed_chunk` is `-1` on a fresh
session.

last_committed_chunk.description: Highest committed chunk index; -1 before the first chunk.

next_chunk.description: The chunk index the next POST must carry.

PushChunkReport.description:
The per-row report of one chunk — the D2 contract shape, kept
Serialize+Deserialize so a committed chunk's stored copy replays
faithfully on an exact re-send.

chunk_index.description:
Position of this chunk in the run. Must be the checkpoint's
`next_chunk`; a lower index replays (same payload) or 409s
(`migration_chunk_reused`, different payload); a higher index 409s
