Wave 41 lane 12: whether the portal shows this status's own label to a
client. Absent = unchanged.

WIP cap (0089): absent = unchanged; JSON `null` = CLEAR the cap; a
number = set it (1..=1000 — the DB CHECK is the backstop).

active.description: Reactivating an archived item is a plain update.

UpdateStockItemRequest.description:
PATCH /api/stock-items/{id}. Absent fields keep their value;
`Some(None)` clears an optional field.

color.description: Some → set (null clears); absent → no change.

PINNED audience — the assertion's `aud` must equal this exactly
(the Access application's AUD tag).

enabled.description:
Deny-by-default: omitted or false creates/keeps the source
DISABLED. Only an explicit admin `true` enables authentication.

issuer.description:
PINNED issuer — the assertion's `iss` must equal this exactly.
For Cloudflare Access: `https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com`.

jwks_url.description: Team JWKS URL the assertion signature is verified against.

client_secret.description: Write-only: stored encrypted at rest, never returned.

preset.description:
Declarative first-party preset (`google` | `entra` | `okta`).
When set, issuer + discovery_url are DERIVED from the preset
template + [`Self::preset_params`]; request values, when also
present, must match the derivation exactly (mix-up defense).

preset_params.description:
Template parameters for the preset (e.g. `tenant` for Entra,
`domain` for Okta).

ValueView.description: One effective value: registry default overlaid by any stored override.

value.description: JSON payload typed by the declaration's kind.

VaultEntryView.description:
A vault entry as the asset detail page sees it: metadata only —
reveal rides the audited `/passwords/{id}/reveal` endpoint.

avg_daily_milli.description: Average daily outbound rate in milli over the window.

window_days.description: Lookback window in days (default 30; outbound legs summed).

account_number.description: The vendor's account number for THIS org.

default_currency.description: ISO 4217 default for POs to this vendor.

VendorContact.description: A typed contact on a vendor.

VendorDetail.description: Vendor detail: the entity plus its typed contacts and external links.

applied.description:
False when the ledger had already recorded this fire (idempotent
replay after a worker retry) — nothing was written or notified.

VerificationCounters.description: The workspace counters that gate the close checklist.

unclassified.description:
Approved + billable + no category slug: these price at the
contract default rate, which is exactly the silent billing the
close ritual exists to catch.

VerificationEntryView.description: One entry inside a ticket group: identity, cost cell, badge.

adjustment_minutes.description: Signed adjustment total (negative or zero; 0 when untouched).

cost_minor.description: Priced cost in contract minor units at the resolved card rate.

disposition.description: The current human disposition, when one was recorded.

effective_minutes.description: Minutes after verification adjustments — what the run will price.

invoiced.description: True when an invoice already consumed this entry (locked).

phase_id.description: Project phase this entry scopes to, when project-scoped.

rate_minor.description: The card rate this entry priced at, per hour.

unbillable_reason.description: Typed unbillable reason when the entry is non-billable.

work_type.description: The category slug, or null (unclassified — a blocker, not a blank).

VerificationGroupView.description: One ticket (or project phase) group with its running totals.

group_id.description:
Stable grouping key: the ticket id, or the phase id for
project-scoped entries (Wave 39 lane 4 gave entries a second
parent, so a phase group has no ticket number).

label.description: Human label: ticket number, else "Project / phase".

total_cost_minor.description: Group cost in contract minor units.

blocks.description:
The block-consumption panel (empty when the contract has no
blocks — retainer overage panels render nothing, not a zero).

overlapping_runs.description: Issued runs whose window overlaps this one (report V8).

preview_total_minor.description:
What the engine says this window would bill. The workspace's
own entry sum and this are computed independently on purpose:
they must agree, and a disagreement is the signal that a
disposition was missed.

oneOf.description: The sign-off recorded for this window, if any.

total_minor.description: Running total across the whole window, in contract minor units.

total_minutes.description: Running total minutes across the window (effective).

VerifyCustomDomainResponse.description: POST `/verify` response: the raw evidence plus the resulting status.

publisher.description:
GitHub `owner/repo` URL or bare path, `registry://slug`, or
a host (zips) — normalized server-side to the publisher identity.

ViewId.description:
Versioned read-model views. Variant ↔ physical view name is frozen
alongside the schema-version suffix; adding a view is additive.

The serde encoding is the view SLUG (`snake_case`) — the same string the
stored-spec `kind` column carries (R3 registry backing) — so a definition
round-trips through JSON without a parallel name table.

project_id.description: Scope to one project's views; omit for the org's ENTIRE view set.

VizHint.description:
Visualization hint the report builder renders with (ADR 0001: Recharts
bar/line/pie/table on the frontend). Pure presentation metadata — it
never influences the compiled SQL.

allOf.description:
Instant-first autosave parameters (IF1): idempotency key +
If-Match `version`.

WarrantyState.description: Which side of the warranty horizon an asset sits on.

WarrantyWindow.description:
The warranty horizon for one device asset: the end date, which side of it
today falls, and how many whole days are left (negative once ended).

challenge_token.description: Opaque ceremony binding — pass back to finish.

label.description: Label shown on the security settings page.

WebhookSecretResponse.description:
Returned by create ONLY — carries the signing secret in plaintext one
final time. There is deliberately no read-back path.

WipLimitUpdate.description:
WIP-cap patch input (0089): `Default` (field absent) = unchanged;
JSON null = clear; a number = set. serde's `Option<Option>` mapping
makes a present-but-null field UNREPRESENTABLE from JSON (null folds
to the outer None), so the three states ride an explicit enum.

WorkNextEntryView.description: One row of a technician's curated queue, as the board renders it.

position.description:
Target rank. Clamped server-side to the queue's bounds: dragging past
the end is a gesture, not a client bug.

user_id.description:
Whose queue to read. Admins may read another technician's (a
dispatcher setting up a shift); anyone may read their own, and a
non-admin asking for someone else is refused rather than silently
served their own.

WorkNextQueueView.description: The whole queue for one technician, in curated order.

display_name.description:
The technician whose queue this is, resolved server-side from the
authenticated principal unless an admin asks for someone else's.

user_id.description:
Absent means "every technician's queue", which is what a placed or
closed ticket needs: its queue entries are stale everywhere at once.

source.description:
`backfill` (the one-time migration mapping) or `manual` (an
admin alias added later).

WorkbenchDecision.description:
The suggestion-grade `decision_record_dedupe` judgment for this
candidate, read from the append-only decision store. `None` (and
therefore silent in the UI) whenever the decision model is
unconfigured — ADR 0010's degrade-quiet posture, never a 5xx.

WorkbenchSide.description:
One side of the workbench comparison: the item view plus its FULL tier
state (observed/curated/field_sources) and identity keys.

WorkflowDocumentView.description:
A workflow document as the canvas reads it. `revision` is the document
version the executor records on each run.

subject_kind.description: `"ticket"` or `"board"` — the tier of subject the document runs against.

WorkflowRetryMode.description: How far back a retry re-executes.

WorkflowRunStatus.description:
What one execution attempt is doing. `Waiting` is the parked state and
is as terminal-as-nothing: it is waiting for a clock or an event, not
for a worker.

WorkflowRunTrigger.description:
Why a run row exists. The two chain kinds are pinned to their pointer
in the database (`workflow_runs_trigger_shape`), so a row can never
claim to be a resume without naming the run it continues.

WorkflowStepStatus.description:
What one step attempt is doing. Wider than the run's because a step can
be SKIPPED: a branch not taken is a recorded fact, not a step that
never happened.

POST /api/auth/email-verification/confirm — marks the email verified
(single-use, audited).

POST /api/auth/email-verification/request — resend (public, THROTTLED;
admin override rides POST /api/org/users/{id}/email-verified).

POST /api/auth/login — resolves the org by email (SECURITY DEFINER
bridge), verifies the argon2 hash under RLS scope. When any second
factor is enrolled, returns a short-lived `mfa_pending` bridge instead
of tokens; POST /api/auth/mfa/verify completes it.
POST /api/auth/logout — revokes the refresh session and audits the event.

POST /api/auth/magic-link/confirm — consumes the link and issues a
full session through the SAME machinery as password login. STAFF
family only (the portal is NOT included — see the threat model).

POST /api/auth/magic-link/request — deny-by-default per org
(`orgs.magic_link_sign_in`, 0088): unknown emails AND disabled orgs
collapse into the SAME uniform answer.

POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery-codes/regenerate — invalidates all previous
codes, issues a new batch (revealed once).

POST /api/auth/mfa/totp/disable — requires password AND a live factor;
wipes TOTP enrollment and all recovery codes.

POST /api/auth/mfa/totp/enroll-begin — generates a secret (returned ONCE)
and stores it sealed+unconfirmed. Re-calling restarts enrollment safely.

POST /api/auth/mfa/totp/enroll-verify — confirms the enrollment with the
first valid code and issues the one-time recovery-code batch.

POST /api/auth/mfa/verify — completes an MFA-gated login with a TOTP or
recovery code. Tries TOTP first (advancing the replay watermark), then
falls back to single-use recovery codes.

POST /api/auth/mfa/webauthn/begin — assertion request for the pending
MFA login. Requires a valid mfa_pending token.

full tokens. Ceremony state is single-use; replay of a finish call fails.

POST /api/auth/mfa/webauthn/register/begin — starts a passkey
registration for the authenticated user.

POST /api/auth/mfa/webauthn/register/finish — verifies the attestation
and stores the passkey. The public key is stored; no secret exists.

replay: the WHOLE chain is revoked and the event is audited.

memory; over the cap the request is a typed 429. A `Last-Event-ID`
header triggers a bounded outbox replay of the events missed while
disconnected (see the resume section above); past the replay buffer
the client falls back to full snapshot rehydration.

parameters.description:
Which audience's slice to return: `human` (the palette) or `ai`
(the LLM tool catalogue). Defaults to `human`.
parameters.name: audience

parameters.description: Restrict to one tier: `a`, `b` or `c`. Defaults to every tier.
parameters.name: tier

parameters.description:
Restrict to one family: `trigger`, `decision`, `condition`,
`action`, `control` or `value`.
parameters.name: family

get.summary:
GET /api/workflows/nodes — the catalogue, filtered. Declarations carry
no org data, so any authed org member may read; each consuming surface
keeps its own data gates.

parameters.description: Node id, e.g. ticket.create
parameters.name: id

get.summary:
GET /api/workflows/nodes/{id} — one node with both schemas parsed.
The on-demand schema leg the authoring model uses, so exposing the
catalogue to a prompt costs one call per node it actually needs rather
than the whole catalogue inlined.

GET /api/workflows/plugin-nodes — the org's plugin-contributed
workflow nodes, parsed through the same contract the registry uses.

parameters.description: Optional status filter: running | waiting | succeeded | failed | abandoned.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Optional rule filter: only that workflow's runs.
parameters.name: rule_id

parameters.description: Cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Page size (default 50, capped at 200).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary:
GET /api/workflows/runs — the run ledger, newest first, filterable by
status and by rule. Keyset-cursored on `(created_at, id)`, exactly like
the webhook delivery ledger: the two logs page and behave alike.
GET /api/workflows/runs/{id} — one run with its whole trace.

post.description:
The refusal is the point: if re-running would repeat a step that
declares `idempotent = false`, the answer is a typed 409 that names every
offending node rather than a second ticket or a second email. The
idempotency key (IF1) is claimed before anything is written, so a
double-submit returns the first retry instead of queueing two.

409.description: not retryable, or a repeat would double-apply

post.summary: POST /api/workflows/runs/{id}/retry — re-run a failed run as a NEW row.

get.summary: GET /api/workflows/runs/{id}/steps — one run's step trace, paged.
